title: Nine-cell ant: does structured shade read better than random shade?
question: Which body reads more like an animal with a front and a top, rather than a block?
context_md:
Both panes are the **same simulation** — same seed, same flat preset, same 600 frames, 15 ants placed, 135 body cells on screen, 9.00 cells per creature in both. **Only the paint differs.**

Each body cell picks a shade from `ant`'s existing **three-colour palette** — the palette is *not* widened, because a wide spread makes a field of cells draw randomly across a range, which is speckle, and speckle destroys the one thing a small body has (its shape).

- One arm gives every cell an **independent random draw**, which is what ships today.
- The other **derives the shade from the cell's place in the body**: palest on the head, then graded pale-on-top to dark-underneath. That is countershading, and it is the only thing that holds contrast against *both* the sky an animal is silhouetted on and the ground it tunnels in.

**What I already measured, and what I am unsure of.** The structured arm puts very slightly *less* luminance on screen (1,270 against 1,295 per creature) — expected, since it deliberately puts pale cells on top where they contrast less with sky. So this is not a contrast win and I am not claiming one. The question is whether the body reads as having an anatomy. I could not judge it myself and the difference may simply be too small to see.

This is a **nine-cell** body because countershading needs a top and a bottom. On the two-cell ant that ships, and on a long single-file chain, there is no underside for the rule to use and the effect is barely visible — measured, and not proposed for the shipped ant.

Separately: nine-cell colonies currently die out within 12,000 frames for reasons unrelated to this, so nothing here is a proposal to ship this body.

items.label: A - random shade (ships today)
items.caption: every cell draws its shade independently

items.label: B - shade by place in the body
items.caption: palest head, pale top, dark underside
